learning_extracted: A null-protection precondition (ceiling-headroom: 'a null in the OFF arm is uninformative') must be branch-scoped in code exactly as pre-registered in prose: applied to the supports branch it converts a positive into substrate_not_ready_requeue. The driver folded it into armed_ok; the docstring scoped it to the falsifying branch.

MAX-across-seeds aggregation of a per-seed readiness quantity turns one anomalous seed into an arm-level kill switch while the criterion it protects already handles seed heterogeneity with a 2/3 majority; per-seed gating (exclude the seed) or mean-aggregation matches the criterion's own granularity.

Seed 44's coupled anomaly (OFF at 0.973 of ceiling; the 'non-propagating' TEMP control diverging 0.686; noise<temp) is a recognisable state: near-uniform committed behaviour makes score vectors near-tie, so ANY perturbation flips argmins and lift comparisons compress. Worth a per-seed saturation exclusion rule in future conversion-lineage drivers.

The raised class floor (one integer, support_preserving_min_first_action_classes=action_dim) did exactly what 708b's third unenumerated reading predicted: OFF fraction-of-ceiling fell from 0.978 (708b, floor 2) to 0.833 mean (floor 5), giving the lineage its first non-degenerate conversion test -- confirming the class-floor ceiling explanation for 708b's precommit_shape_headroom_unexplained (GFLAG-0072 context).

Reanalysis, not re-run: every readout needed to overturn the self-route is already in the manifest per-seed; a 955a re-queue would spend ~13h of hub compute to re-derive data in hand (GOV-REUSE-1 spirit).

Hygiene (red-team, non-verdict-moving): manifest carries substrate_stable_across_run=false from the known driver-in-hash-toggle false-positive class (A0_OFF fingerprint hashes without the driver, lever arms with it) -- no real substrate drift, but it makes the banked A0_OFF baseline mint REFUSE_SUBSTRATE_UNSTABLE-ineligible for reuse; the driver's 'elif A0_OFF not in green' branch is unreachable given armed_ok's definition.
